latitude.why: Surface (transient strip vs modal vs persistent badge), open semantics (new window vs in-place swap), display order, and overflow policy are all reviewer-debatable; only flock ownership, the adoption default, and env-free operation are forced.

q1.position: A single modal session picker on Ctrl+Shift+S, built like lang_picker: centred, keyboard-owning, mouse-clickable. No first-paint strip; the window title and F1 help carry the pointer to it.
q1.rationale: The modal-picker pattern is proven in this file; one surface to build, translate, and maintain.

q2.position: Active summon with a passive breadcrumb: window_title becomes 'terminal-delight — 2 (+2 saved)' whenever other free sessions exist, and the help modal gains a chord row in all nine language packs.
q2.rationale: The title already names the held session; extending it breaks the silence without painting a banner over terminals.

q3.position: Per row: id, tab count plus pane count, absolute saved timestamp, and the last_workspace hint. Tab count comes from cheaply counting '[[tabs]]' headers during the existing scan — read-only, no format change.
q3.rationale: A full-screen modal has room for the richer identification the ticket's mock gestures at ('2 tabs').

q4.position: Chord opens the modal listing sessions newest-first; arrows and Enter (or click) choose one. TD claims the target's flock, saves and releases the current session, then rebuilds this same window from the target's StateFile.
q4.rationale: One window, no proliferation: 'open the other one' replaces the wrong adoption instead of adding a sibling.

q5.position: Replaced in place: the current session is saved to disk and its lock released, then the window restores the target. Requires making instance's process binding rebindable — Bound's key behind a mutex, not set-once.
q5.rationale: The named refactor is the honest cost of in-place switching; the boot-time restore code already exists to reuse.

q6.position: The flock stays the arbiter: claim the target BEFORE saving and releasing the current session; on failure show 'session is now live elsewhere' and stay put. Held sessions render greyed and unopenable.
q6.rationale: Claim-first ordering means a lost race costs nothing; the kernel lock still guarantees exclusivity.

q7.position: The chord always opens the modal; with zero or one saved session it shows only the current session plus a 'no other saved sessions' line. The title suffix appears only when others exist.
q7.rationale: A summonable surface can afford an empty state; the passive hint stays strictly conditional.

q8.position: Pure recency: saved mtime descending, id as tiebreak, matching the ticket's sketch. rank()'s workspace and substantial keys are adoption policy, not what a human browsing a list expects.
q8.rationale: Newest-first is the universal list convention; rank() itself is untouched, satisfying the scope line.

q9.position: The modal shows 9 rows, then becomes a scrollable list with an 'N sessions' footer; the underlying list is never truncated.
q9.rationale: Nine rows fill a centred modal comfortably at default size; scroll handles the pathological long tail.

q10.position: Stateless: the modal rescans sessions on every open, and the title suffix recomputes on each save. Nothing introduced by this feature is persisted anywhere.
q10.rationale: Disk state (tomls plus locks) is authoritative; a persisted cache could only disagree with it.

q11.position: Yes: chord, arrows, Enter — entirely in-process. No environment variable is involved anywhere in this path, not even internally, since no child process is spawned.
q11.rationale: In-place switching is the only design where even the internal plumbing is env-free.

q12.position: Yes — cold launch still silently adopts via untouched resolve_session; switching is strictly a post-launch, user-summoned action that runs after adoption has completed.
q12.rationale: The default path gains only a title suffix; its behaviour and ranking are byte-for-byte unchanged.
